title: Varonis documents TheMailer, a self-hosted phishing kit that uses commercial AI models to reach inboxes
date_note: Publication date not stated on the Varonis page; the earliest date available is when this record was first seen (19 November); TechRadar's article is dated 22 November.
summary: Varonis Threat Labs describes TheMailer, a self-hosted phishing platform sold with a lifetime licence of $3,000 to $6,000. It uses operator-supplied keys for AI services to rewrite lures, send test emails and retry until they reach the inbox. An Autopilot screenshot shows a list of 145,133 entries, nearly all Japanese .co.jp and .ac.jp domains.
plain: A phishing kit sold to criminals uses AI chatbots to rewrite scam emails until spam filters let them through.
exec: Varonis says the kit rewrites messages that spam filters block and retries delivery; TechRadar notes this makes detection based on identical templates less reliable.
action: Varonis advises enforcing SPF, DKIM and DMARC at p=reject and checking links through their full redirect chain at click time.

validation.note: Varonis' own write-up and TechRadar (22 Nov, citing Varonis Threat Labs) both describe the kit; TechRadar relays Varonis, so the vendor's own page remains the primary. Vendor also promotes its own product.
